traits.label: Hymenium
traits.text: Gills that are decurrent, rather spaced, yellowish turning olive-brown with age.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Hymenium: Gills that are decurrent, rather spaced, yellowish turning olive-brown with age.

traits.label: Cap
traits.text: Initially convex, later becoming flattened or slightly depressed in the center, slimy and sticky when wet, yellowish to orange-brown, often with a darker center.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Cap: Initially convex, later becoming flattened or slightly depressed in the center, slimy and sticky when wet, yellowish to orange-brown, often with a darker center.

traits.label: Hymenium Attachment
traits.text: Decurrent.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Hymenium Attachment: Decurrent.

traits.label: Stipe
traits.text: Cylindrical, often tapered towards the base, white at the top and yellowish to reddish-brown downwards, covered in a gelatinous veil when young.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Stipe: Cylindrical, often tapered towards the base, white at the top and yellowish to reddish-brown downwards, covered in a gelatinous veil when young.

traits.label: Dimensions
traits.text: Cap: 5-10 cm in diameter.
traits.raw: 📐 Cap: 5-10 cm in diameter.

traits.label: Fruit body
traits.text: Fruit body: 7-15 cm tall.
traits.raw: 📏 Fruit body: 7-15 cm tall.

traits.label: Spore print
traits.text: Spore Print: Dark olive-brown.
traits.raw: 🟤 Spore Print: Dark olive-brown.

traits.label: Ecology
traits.text: Mycorrhizal, particularly associated with conifers such as spruces and pines.
traits.raw: 🌲 Mycorrhizal, particularly associated with conifers such as spruces and pines.

traits.label: Edibility
traits.text: Edible, though not highly regarded due to its slimy texture.
traits.raw: 🍴 Edible, though not highly regarded due to its slimy texture.

traits.label: Microscopy
traits.text: Spores 17-22 x 5-6.5 µm, elliptical and smooth.
traits.raw: 🔬 Spores 17-22 x 5-6.5 µm, elliptical and smooth.

traits.label: Odour
traits.text: Not distinctive.
traits.raw: 👃 Not distinctive.

traits.label: Overview
traits.text: Distinguished by its notably slimy cap and its association with coniferous trees. The decurrent gills and the gelatinous veil on the stipe are also defining features.
traits.raw: 🔤 Distinguished by its notably slimy cap and its association with coniferous trees. The decurrent gills and the gelatinous veil on the stipe are also defining features.

🍄 Gomphidiaceae / Agaricomycetes

ℹ️ Hymenium: Gills that are decurrent, rather spaced, yellowish turning olive-brown with age.
ℹ️ Cap: Initially convex, later becoming flattened or slightly depressed in the center, slimy and sticky when wet, yellowish to orange-brown, often with a darker center.
ℹ️ Hymenium Attachment: Decurrent.
ℹ️ Stipe: Cylindrical, often tapered towards the base, white at the top and yellowish to reddish-brown downwards, covered in a gelatinous veil when young.
📐 Cap: 5-10 cm in diameter.
📏 Fruit body: 7-15 cm tall.
🟤 Spore Print: Dark olive-brown.
🌲 Mycorrhizal, particularly associated with conifers such as spruces and pines.
🍴 Edible, though not highly regarded due to its slimy texture.
🔬 Spores 17-22 x 5-6.5 µm, elliptical and smooth.
👃 Not distinctive.
🔤 Distinguished by its notably slimy cap and its association with coniferous trees. The decurrent gills and the gelatinous veil on the stipe are also defining features.
